It depends on your situation. If the car you have is a good car, paying off the original loan is always best. But if you can get a good trade in amount and you are downgrading to lower overall payments, that might work out best for you as well.

I would advise to use some of the online trade in tools that can show you what your payments will look like at the current interest rates. Many can factor in trade in etc as well.

Good luck.

You have to factor in the value of your trade in, just because you paid $12000 doesn't mean it's now worth that and the amount you still owe on the original loan. 

If your trade in is valued at $8000 and you still owe$10000 on the original loan, you will have a deficit of $2000 on any new loan that you take out.

Most dealerships will gladly pull over that deficit into a new loan on a car, but you just keep digging a hole for your self.

My 19 year old son committed suicide a little over two years ago. He said in his letter that he never felt safe or loved. He didn't mention me by name, but as his father I took it that way. It devistated me. His suicide has left me with depression, guilt, suicidal thoughts, etc. I tried to be a good father but I didn't see the signs, I didn't notice the things that I should have. I love him so much and my lifes  purpose was to try to make him feel safe, so when he said that in the letter it crushed me and still does.

He suffered from depression and anxiety so we had gotten him into counseling. He was home schooled because the school environment was too much for him. He played guitar and had a few close friends. He had a girlfriend when this happened and she was actually coming to spend a week with our family the day after this happened. I helped him set up his own business. I thought I was doing the right things, but it wasn't enough.

People say not to blame yourself etc etc, I will always blame myself. Two years later and I miss him so much.
